content.title: About
content.content: The Roast Beef Sandwich on white (1726) is a classic sandwich featuring thinly sliced roast beef placed between two slices of soft white bread. It is often complemented with lettuce, tomato slices, mustard or mayo, creating a balanced and flavorful bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Roast beef is a slow‑roasted cut of beef, traditionally from the rib or sirloin, cooked at low temperature.
Roast beef sandwiches are popular in the US and the UK, commonly served in cafés and bistros.
White bread used in this sandwich is typically soft and crust‑less, highlighting the tenderness of the meat.
The beef is sliced against the grain to ensure a tender chew.
The sandwich is often served with pickles or sauerkraut for a flavor contrast.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Roast beef provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: When served on white bread, the sandwich offers a moderate amount of carbohydrates suitable for balanced meals.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc from beef supports immune health and wound healing.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Condiments such as mustard or mayo can raise the salt level of the sandwich.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef contains saturated fat; individuals with cardiovascular concerns should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: White bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor harmful bacteria; use reputable sources and store properly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. Add lettuce, cucumber slices, pickles or crispy bacon for extra texture and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Store roast beef separately, wrapped tightly, to prevent drying out.
